chapters.title: Welcome: How This Book Works
chapters.sub: The loop, the page legend, the map, and the habits that make everything else easier
goals: Use the copy buttons, placeholder chips, practice terminal and in-page Python
Follow the learning loop: read five minutes, type five minutes, break something, fix it, build one thing
Find any chapter or command from the map of the book
Read an error message and a man page without panic
Apply the two golden rules before running any command

chapters.title: Setting Up Your Lab
chapters.sub: Terminal, zsh, Homebrew, Python, PyCharm and the ~/lab practice folder
goals: Configure Terminal and confirm that the shell is zsh
Install the Xcode command line tools and Homebrew, and put Homebrew on your PATH
Install the networking and text tools the book uses with one brew command
Create a PyCharm project with its own virtual environment and run a Python file two ways
Create ~/lab with the Lab Kit and fill in My Values from your own network

chapters.title: How Computers Work
chapters.sub: Bits, bytes, text encodings, processes, system calls and how the shell finds a command
goals: Convert numbers between binary, decimal and hexadecimal by hand and in code
Explain how text is stored as bytes in ASCII and UTF-8
Describe what the kernel, a process, a system call and a file descriptor are
Tell a terminal from a shell and a compiled program from a script
Predict which program runs when you type a command, using PATH and exit status

chapters.title: How Networks Work
chapters.sub: Layers, encapsulation, Ethernet, IP, TCP, DHCP, ARP, DNS, NAT, HTTP and TLS, with a read-only command at every step
goals: Name the layers of the TCP/IP and OSI models and the unit of data at each one
Explain how a packet is wrapped at each layer and what changes at every hop
Describe what DHCP, ARP, DNS, NAT and the TCP handshake each do, and in what order
Walk through a web request from URL to page and name the tool that observes each step
Read ifconfig, arp, netstat -rn, dig and curl -v output and label the layers in it

chapters.title: Addressing & Subnetting
chapters.sub: Read any IP, mask, MAC or routing-table line and do the subnet maths in your head and in Python
goals: Convert between dotted decimal, binary, hex and prefix-length forms of an address and a mask
Compute network, broadcast, first, last and usable hosts with the magic-number method
Split a block with VLSM and summarize several blocks into one route
Predict which routing-table entry wins using longest-prefix match
Read IPv6 addresses, MAC addresses and the netmask that macOS prints in hex
Build ipcalc.py, a subnet calculator in pure maths and with the ipaddress module

chapters.title: Thinking Like a Programmer
chapters.sub: Decompose problems, pick the right algorithm and data structure, debug on purpose and keep history with git
goals: Break a vague task into steps and write it as pseudocode or an ASCII flowchart
Explain linear versus binary search and what O(n) and O(log n) mean, with measurements
Choose between a list, dictionary, set, stack, queue, tree and graph for a networking task
Debug with the loop reproduce, isolate, hypothesize, test, and read an error message from the bottom up
Track your work in a git repository with branches, merges and a remote
Edit a file with nano and get out of vim alive

chapters.title: zsh Fundamentals
chapters.sub: How the shell reads a line, finds a program, expands what you type, remembers it and starts up
goals: Take a command line apart into command, options and arguments, and say which part the shell handles
Find out what a name resolves to (alias, function, builtin or file) and why one thing shadows another
Predict the result of quoting, globbing, brace, tilde and parameter expansion before pressing Return
Use glob qualifiers and extended globs to select files by type, age and size
Edit and recall command lines with emacs keys, history expansion and search
Build a ~/.zshrc with options, history, prompt, completion, aliases and a function

chapters.title: Files, Folders & Permissions
chapters.sub: Navigate the macOS filesystem, move and find things, archive and verify them, and control who can touch what
goals: Explain what lives where on a Mac and read any absolute or relative path
Create, copy, move, link and delete files and folders without losing data
Find files by name, type, size and age with find, mdfind and zsh globs
Archive, compress and checksum a folder and verify the copy
Read ls -l and set permissions with chmod, in symbolic and octal form
Recover from Permission denied and Operation not permitted by diagnosing the cause

chapters.title: Streams, Redirection & Pipes
chapters.sub: How commands pass data to each other, and how you wire them together
goals: Explain stdin, stdout and stderr and redirect each one on its own
Chain commands with pipes and read a pipeline from left to right
Feed one command's output into another command's arguments with $(), xargs and <()
Use exit codes, &&, || and pipefail so chains fail safely
Build a five-stage pipeline from scratch against real log data

chapters.title: The Text-Processing Toolkit
chapters.sub: grep, sort, sed, awk, jq and friends: reshape any text into the answer you need
goals: Select lines with grep and write regular expressions in BRE, ERE and Python-style flavours
Count, rank and de-duplicate data with sort, uniq and wc
Cut, join, compare and reformat text with cut, tr, paste, join, comm, diff and column
Edit streams with sed substitutions, addresses and capture groups
Write awk programs with fields, patterns, arrays and printf to sum, group and report
Turn messy logs, CSV and JSON into answers using multi-stage pipelines

chapters.title: Shell Scripting in zsh
chapters.sub: Variables, tests, loops, functions and options: turn one-liners into tools, and build netcheck.zsh
goals: Write an executable zsh script with a shebang, arguments, exit codes and a place on your PATH
Use variables, arrays, associative arrays and parameter expansion correctly under zsh's rules
Branch and loop with [[ ]], if, case, for, while and select, and read input line by line
Structure code with functions, local variables and getopts or zparseopts option parsing
Make scripts fail safely with setopt, trap and cleanup, and debug them with xtrace
Build netcheck.zsh, a coloured network health report that exits non-zero on failure

chapters.title: System, Processes & macOS Tools
chapters.sub: See what your Mac is running, stop it safely, and query hardware, disks, logs and settings from the shell
goals: Explain what a process is and read ps, top and lsof output
Stop, pause and restart processes with signals, and manage background jobs in zsh
Inspect services with launchctl and packages with brew
Query hardware, OS, memory, disks and power with sysctl, system_profiler, diskutil, vm_stat and pmset
Read and write settings with defaults and read logs with log show
Combine these tools into a one-screen sysinfo.zsh report

chapters.title: See Your Own Network
chapters.sub: Read every field macOS tells you about interfaces, addresses, routes, neighbours and DNS, and pipe it into variables
goals: Read an ifconfig block field by field and say what each line means
Tell which interface carries your traffic and why, using the routing table
Extract your IP, MAC, gateway, DNS servers and prefix length into shell variables
Recognise utun, awdl, bridge and link-local entries without panicking
List the neighbours on your LAN from the ARP cache and turn them into a CSV

chapters.title: Reachability, Latency & Path
chapters.sub: Measure whether a host answers, how long it takes, where the packets travel and how big they can be
goals: Read ping output and statistics and explain every number in them
Use traceroute and mtr to locate where on a path latency or loss starts
Compute average, jitter, loss and 95th percentile of round-trip times with awk
Find the path MTU to a host with ping and the Don't Fragment bit
Build latency-log, a script that records round-trip times to CSV and summarises them

chapters.title: DNS: Names, Records & Resolvers
chapters.sub: Resolve names with dig, nslookup, host and the macOS resolver, read every record type, and spot DNS problems fast
goals: Explain the path of a lookup from the stub resolver to an authoritative server
Read all sections of a dig answer, including flags, status and TTL
Query a specific resolver or an authoritative server directly and compare answers
Predict which macOS tools honour /etc/hosts, search domains and per-domain resolvers
Build dnscheck, a script that reports A, MX, NS and TXT records and compares public resolvers

chapters.title: HTTP and TLS
chapters.sub: Read, send and time web requests by hand with curl, and inspect the certificates behind https
goals: Read an HTTP request and response line by line and name the job of each header you meet
Fetch, filter and time any URL with curl, and choose the flags that make it safe in scripts
Follow a redirect chain and explain 301, 302, 303, 307 and 308 by what they do to the method
Split one request's time into DNS, TCP, TLS, server wait and download with curl -w
Read a certificate with openssl and check how many days it has left
Practice against a web server you run yourself, then against the public internet

chapters.title: Ports and Scanning
chapters.sub: See which programs listen on your Mac, test ports with nc, and map your own LAN with nmap, ethically
goals: Explain sockets, ports and the five-part tuple that identifies a connection
Read TCP states in netstat output and say what CLOSE_WAIT or TIME_WAIT piles mean
Find which process owns a port with lsof, and free the port safely
Test, listen on and transfer data over a port with nc
Run host-discovery and port scans with nmap on networks you own, and parse the results with awk
Build lan-inventory, a script that turns your LAN into a CSV of hosts and services

chapters.title: Packet Capture
chapters.sub: Record your own traffic with tcpdump and Wireshark, read it line by line, and filter it down to the packets you care about
goals: Capture and read your own traffic with tcpdump, including the handshake, DNS and ARP
Write BPF capture filters and display filters, and say which tool uses which
Decode a tcpdump line field by field: timestamp, endpoints, flags, sequence numbers, window, length
Save a capture to a .pcap file and analyze it later with tcpdump, tshark and Wireshark
Turn live or saved packets into counts and lists with grep, awk and tshark fields
Annotate a packet trace and explain what each packet is doing

chapters.title: Remote Access with SSH
chapters.sub: Log in, copy files and tunnel traffic to another machine over an encrypted channel, with keys instead of passwords
goals: Explain how SSH authenticates the server and the user, and what known_hosts protects you from
Create an ed25519 key pair, install the public key on a server and use ssh-agent and the macOS Keychain
Write a ~/.ssh/config that turns long commands into one-word aliases, including a jump host
Copy files with scp, sftp and rsync and avoid the trailing-slash and --delete traps
Build local, remote and dynamic tunnels and say which one a situation needs
Harden an SSH server so only your key gets in, without locking yourself out

chapters.title: Troubleshooting a Network
chapters.sub: Find the broken layer in five minutes, fix it, and build netdoctor.zsh to do the walking for you
goals: Walk the stack bottom-up (link, address, gateway, internet, DNS, transport, application) with one command per layer
Recognize the common failure signatures from their exact output
Apply the right fix and know which fixes need sudo and which are risky
Split a slow request into DNS, TCP, TLS and server time with curl -w
Extend netcheck.zsh into netdoctor.zsh, which stops at the first broken layer and suggests a fix

chapters.title: Python Start: Interpreter, Environments & PyCharm
chapters.sub: Install, run, isolate and debug your first Python programs in Terminal and PyCharm
goals: Identify which Python your Mac runs and why, and avoid touching Apple's copy
Use the REPL and run code with python3 file.py, -c and -m
Create, activate and rebuild a virtual environment with venv and pip
Create a PyCharm project, pick its interpreter and use Run, the Terminal and the Python Console
Read input with input(), print results and build a small stdin-driven units tool

chapters.title: Python Basics: Numbers, Text & Operators
chapters.sub: Values, types, strings, bytes and the operators that connect them, with a reference card for every built-in and string method
goals: Choose the right numeric type and predict the result of //, %, ** and rounding
Slice, search and format strings, including the f-string format-spec mini-language
Convert between str and bytes and explain what an encoding does
Use comparison, logical, bitwise, membership and identity operators and know their precedence
Apply an IP mask with bitwise operators and convert values safely between types

chapters.title: Python Flow: Decisions, Loops & Functions
chapters.sub: Make programs choose, repeat and reuse code, and package it as a command-line script
goals: Write if/elif/else, conditional expressions and match statements
Choose between for, while, break, continue and loop-else, and use range, enumerate and zip
Define functions with defaults, keyword-only parameters, *args and **kwargs, and return several values
Predict variable scope with LEGB and avoid the mutable-default trap
Structure a script with main(), __name__ and sys.argv

chapters.title: Python Data Structures: Lists, Dicts, Sets & Collections
chapters.sub: Store, group, count and sort data with the right container, then summarize a web log in a few lines
goals: Choose between list, tuple, dict, set and frozenset by asking about order, mutability and lookup
Slice, unpack and copy sequences without tripping over aliasing
Write list, dict, set and generator comprehensions and read nested ones
Sort by one or several keys with sorted(), key= and a stable sort
Count, group and rank data with Counter, defaultdict, deque and namedtuple
Build the core of loganalyzer.py: parse log lines into records and summarize them

chapters.title: Python Files, Text & Regular Expressions
chapters.sub: Read and write files, parse CSV, JSON, dates and logs with re, and make Python behave in a shell pipeline
goals: Open, read, write and close files safely with with, in text and binary mode
Manipulate paths with pathlib and know when to reach for os, shutil and glob
Read and write CSV and JSON, and parse timestamps with datetime
Write regular expressions with groups, named groups, flags and lazy quantifiers, and apply them with re
Write a Python tool that reads stdin, writes stdout, reports errors on stderr and sets an exit status
Finish loganalyzer.py as a stdin-to-stdout command-line tool

chapters.title: Errors, Debugging & Testing
chapters.sub: Handle failures on purpose, read any traceback, step through code with pdb and PyCharm, and prove your functions work with tests
goals: Read a traceback from the bottom up and name the frame that holds the bug
Catch, raise, chain and define exceptions with try, except, else, finally and raise from
Choose between EAFP and LBYL and validate network data without crashing on the first bad line
Replace debugging prints with logging, breakpoint() and pdb commands
Debug in PyCharm with breakpoints, conditions, stepping, watches and Evaluate Expression
Write unittest and pytest tests and drive a function with a test-first loop

chapters.title: Modules, Packages & Command-Line Tools
chapters.sub: Split code into modules and packages, isolate dependencies with venv and pip, and ship real tools with argparse
goals: Explain what import does, where Python looks for modules, and fix ModuleNotFoundError and shadowing
Build a package with __init__.py, relative imports and a __main__.py
Create a virtual environment, install packages on macOS under PEP 668, and pin them in requirements.txt or pyproject.toml
Use the standard library confidently by knowing which module solves which problem
Write command-line tools with argparse: arguments, types, choices, flags, subcommands, exit codes
Turn ipcalc.py into an installable package with its own command and tests

chapters.title: Classes, Objects & Idiomatic Python
chapters.sub: Model hosts, ports and networks as types, then use dunder methods, dataclasses, generators, decorators and context managers
goals: Write classes with attributes, methods, properties, class methods and static methods
Make your own objects behave like built-ins with dunder methods such as __repr__, __eq__, __len__, __iter__ and __contains__
Choose between a plain class, a dataclass, an Enum and inheritance or composition for a given model
Build lazy generator pipelines that mirror shell pipelines
Write decorators and context managers, with and without arguments
Read and write basic type hints, including Optional values and Protocols
Assemble netmodel.py, the object model for the netkit capstone

chapters.title: Python for Networking
chapters.sub: Sockets, struct, threads and subprocess: write your own client, server, scanner and monitor
goals: Write a TCP echo server and client and explain why TCP is a byte stream
Send and receive UDP datagrams and see why silence is the only error you get
Parse a raw IPv4 and TCP header from hex with struct
Scan ports in parallel with threads and a connect timeout
Fetch web data with urllib, http.client and ssl, and drive ping and dig with subprocess
Build portscan.py, a scanner that refuses targets outside your own network

chapters.title: How the Web Works: Browsers, Servers and Your First Page
chapters.sub: What a browser and a web server do on every page load, how URLs and origins work, and a first site you write, serve and inspect on your Mac
goals: Name the parts of a browser and say which part handles the network, HTML, CSS and JavaScript
Take a URL apart, resolve a relative link and build a query string with new URL() and URLSearchParams
Follow one page load from DNS lookup to first paint and say which phase slow Wi-Fi or a slow server stretches
Tell static pages, server-side rendering, client-side rendering and JSON APIs apart, and explain the same-origin rule that governs them
Write a two-page site in Terminal, serve it with python3 -m http.server and inspect it with Safari or Chrome DevTools
Watch requests to the practice server in a Network pane and read their status and headers

chapters.title: HTML: Structure, Semantics and Forms
chapters.sub: Write documents that browsers, screen readers and servers all understand: the skeleton, the parse tree, semantic elements, links, images, tables and forms that send data
goals: Write a correct document skeleton and say what every line of the head does
Predict the DOM tree the parser builds, including how it repairs bad nesting, and check it in Elements
Mark up a page with landmarks, an ordered heading outline, lists, links, images and an accessible data table
Build forms with the right input types, labels and built-in validation, and say exactly what the browser sends for GET, POST and multipart
Use id, class and data-* attributes for their separate jobs and apply the core accessibility rules
Choose between classic, defer, async and module scripts

chapters.title: CSS: Selectors, the Cascade, the Box Model and Layout
chapters.sub: Attach styles, target exactly the elements you mean, predict which rule wins, size boxes, and lay out a responsive dashboard with a dark theme
goals: Attach CSS to a page and read any rule as selector, declarations, properties and values
Target elements with class, attribute, combinator and pseudo-class selectors, including :is(), :where() and :has()
Predict the winning declaration from origin, specificity, order and inheritance, and fix a losing rule without !important
Size boxes with the box model and lay them out with flexbox, grid and positioning
Make a dashboard responsive with media queries and clamp(), and theme it with custom properties
Find out why an element looks the way it does with the Elements pane and getComputedStyle()

chapters.title: JavaScript Fundamentals
chapters.sub: Values, types, operators, strings, arrays, objects and JSON, with the traps that catch Python programmers
goals: Run JavaScript in a jsrun box, the browser console and Node.js in Terminal
Predict how JavaScript stores numbers, compares values with == and ===, and decides truthiness
Declare variables with let and const and explain block scope, hoisting and the temporal dead zone
Process strings, arrays and objects with built-in methods chained into pipelines
Convert data to and from JSON and say what does not survive the trip

chapters.title: JavaScript in Depth: Functions, Objects, Modules and Async
chapters.sub: Closures, this, prototypes and classes, iterators, errors, modules, the event loop, promises, fetch and regular expressions
goals: Explain closures and predict what this refers to in any call
Model data with prototypes and classes, including private fields, accessors and static factories
Split code into ES modules and explain why the browser loads them only over HTTP
Predict the output order of synchronous code, microtasks and timers
Fetch JSON with status checks, timeouts and retries using promises and async/await
Parse and rewrite text with JavaScript regular expressions and named groups

chapters.title: Browser DevTools and the Console
chapters.sub: Open the developer tools in Safari and Chrome, drive any page from the Console, read the Network waterfall, inspect storage, and debug JavaScript with breakpoints instead of guesses
goals: Open Web Inspector in Safari and DevTools in Chrome, and pick the panel that answers your question
Use the Console API (format specifiers, table, group, count, assert, time) and the console utilities ($0, $$, $x, copy, inspect)
Scrape and change a live page from the Console and turn the result into JSON for Terminal
Read a request in the Network pane, from status and headers to timing phases, and replay it with fetch or curl
Debug a script with line, conditional and DOM breakpoints, stepping, Scope and the call stack
Inspect and edit localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies, and know what HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite protect

chapters.title: The DOM: Selecting, Changing and Listening
chapters.sub: Treat a page as a live tree of objects you can query, rewrite and wire to events, without opening an XSS hole
goals: Walk the node tree and pick elements with getElementById, querySelector(All), closest and matches
Change text, attributes, classes and styles, and explain why textContent beats innerHTML for untrusted data
Build and insert elements in batches with createElement, append, DocumentFragment and template cloning
Handle events with options, propagation and delegation, including a form that POSTs to an API
Render lists from fetched data with loading, empty and error states, polling and debounced search
Persist small UI state in localStorage and react to changes with MutationObserver and IntersectionObserver

chapters.title: XML and Friends: Parsing, XPath, SVG, RSS and plists
chapters.sub: Read, query, build, validate and transform XML in the browser and in Terminal, and know when XML is the right format
goals: Write well-formed XML with declarations, attributes, escaping, CDATA, comments and namespaces
Parse XML in the browser with DOMParser, detect parser errors and serialise documents back to text
Query documents with XPath 1.0 in the browser, in DevTools with $x() and in Terminal with xmllint
Fetch and render an RSS feed and a device inventory, and build XML safely with DOM methods
Draw a live status chart with SVG elements created by createElementNS
Inspect, convert and query macOS property lists, and explain XXE and entity-expansion attacks

chapters.title: Node.js: JavaScript on the Server
chapters.sub: Run JavaScript outside the browser: scripts in zsh pipelines, files and processes, a web server from scratch, npm, Express and tests
goals: Install a current Node LTS on the Mac and use the REPL, scripts, arguments, environment variables and exit codes
Tell ES modules from CommonJS and fix the errors each one produces
Read and write files, stream a log through a Node script inside a zsh pipeline, and run other programs without shell injection
Build a JSON API on node:http, then rebuild it with Express middleware
Manage packages and scripts with npm, and read semver ranges and the lockfile
Configure a server with .env, answer CORS preflights, debug with --inspect and test with node --test

chapters.title: Server Basics: Services, Logs and Reverse Proxies
chapters.sub: Run servers on your Mac, look inside the request loop, keep services alive with launchd and systemd, read logs, and route requests with nginx
goals: Explain what makes a process a server and choose the right bind address for it
Write and test a JSON API with the standard library, and test application code without a network
Keep a server running with a LaunchAgent on macOS or a systemd unit on Linux, and read its logs
Secure a fresh Linux server in the first fifteen minutes without locking yourself out
Name the failing layer from the symptom a client sees, and predict which nginx location answers a request

chapters.title: APIs: Calling, Designing and Securing Web APIs
chapters.sub: Call REST APIs from curl, JavaScript and Python, read every status and header, authenticate safely, page, retry and rate-limit, and verify webhooks
goals: Read any API response by its status class, headers and body, and choose the right status for your own endpoints
Call APIs from JavaScript and Python with error handling that refuses to ignore failures
Explain API keys, bearer tokens, JWTs and OAuth with PKCE, and keep secrets out of code and history
Page through large collections, retry only what is safe, and respect rate limits with backoff
Design a predictable REST API with one error format and an OpenAPI description, and verify signed webhooks

chapters.title: Encryption: Hashes, Keys, Signatures and TLS
chapters.sub: Break a classical cipher, use hashes, MACs, AES-GCM and signatures correctly, build your own certificate authority and read a TLS 1.3 handshake
goals: Tell encoding, hashing, MACs, encryption and signatures apart, and choose the right one for a job
Verify downloads with SHA-256 and store passwords with a salted, slow hash
Encrypt and decrypt with AES-GCM, and explain why a reused nonce is catastrophic
Explain key exchange and signatures, and sign and verify files with your SSH key
Build a private CA, serve HTTPS with it, and read every step of a TLS 1.3 handshake

chapters.title: Cloud Computing: Compute, Storage, Networks and IAM
chapters.sub: Choose between VMs, containers and functions, plan a VPC, lock down access with IAM, describe it all as code and keep the bill under control
goals: Explain IaaS, PaaS, SaaS and functions, and where the shared-responsibility line falls for each
Containerise a service and run it locally with the right port and bind address
Plan VPC address space and predict reachability from routes, public IPs and security groups
Read and write IAM policies, and explain how explicit deny, allow and default deny combine
Describe infrastructure as code with Terraform or OpenTofu, and keep a learning account safe and cheap

chapters.title: Capstone: netkit
chapters.sub: Build one tested, installable command that combines subnet maths, ping, DNS, port scan and log analysis
goals: Structure a Python project as an installable package with a src layout and pyproject.toml
Build a multi-command CLI with argparse subcommands and shared options
Separate parsing, networking and presentation so each piece can be tested alone
Write pytest tests for pure functions, a real loopback socket and the CLI itself
Make a tool behave in pipelines with exit codes, quiet mode, stdin and JSON or CSV output
Review your own code against a rubric

chapters.title: Capstone: a LAN Dashboard, Front to Back
chapters.sub: Build, test, debug and share a full-stack app: Express API, JSON file store, TCP port checks, XML and RSS feeds, and a plain-JavaScript dashboard
goals: Structure a Node project so the API, the storage, the network checks and the feeds can each be tested alone
Build a REST API with validation errors a form can display, backed by a JSON file written atomically
Check device ports with net.Socket and a timeout, only on your own LAN, and publish changes as events and RSS
Write a dashboard front end from semantic HTML, a CSS grid with dark and light themes, and three JavaScript modules
Test the API with node --test against a real server on a random port, and find a planted bug with DevTools
Run the app safely on your Mac and, deliberately, on your LAN

chapters.title: Where to Go From Here
chapters.sub: A map of what you can do now, what to learn next, and a routine that gets you there
goals: List the skills you now have and the chapter where each one lives
Choose one next track (security, Linux, packet crafting, automation, Python depth or web development) and a first project for it
Keep a weekly practice routine that fits around other things
Read primary documentation (man pages, PEPs, RFCs) instead of searching for summaries
Practice offensive skills only on systems built or authorized for it

chapters.title: Cheat Sheets
chapters.sub: One-page lookup tables for the shell, networking, HTTP, permissions, Python, pip, git and web development
goals: Look up a shell, zsh or networking command by task in under a minute
Read a subnet, port, status code or permission value straight from a table
Recall Python syntax, built-ins and venv commands without leaving the terminal
Copy a ready-made pipeline from the quick-recipes section and adapt it
Find a JavaScript, DOM, DevTools, Node.js, XPath or CSS idiom in seconds

chapters.title: Fixes
chapters.sub: A problem-to-fix index for the errors you will actually hit on a Mac
goals: Match an error message to its cause in under a minute
Apply the fix as copyable commands without making things worse
Prevent the common errors in your setup instead of repeating the fix
